model_interface.template_input: FP32 normalized crop tensor [N_templates=1, B=1, C=3, H=256, W=256]
model_interface.template_output: Python dict containing six stage-dependent tensors: cross_block_0 through cross_block_5
model_interface.search_input: FP32 normalized crop tensor [B=1, C=3, H=256, W=256] plus the six-tensor template cache
model_interface.search_encoder_output: temporal feature tensor xz [T, B, C, H, W] consumed by the decoder
model_interface.tracker_output: one Python bbox list [x,y,w,h]; boxes.txt serializes integer truncation
model_interface.fixed_dimensions: I0 freezes batch=1, template count=1, template/search crops=256x256, and decoder feature grid=16x16
model_interface.dynamic_dimensions: source frame size and sequence length are outside the model graph; cache tensor shapes are stage-dependent

state_and_dependencies: Template initialization is a separate encoder call; its six-entry cache is required by every search forward.
The tracker carries the prior bbox in Python state to construct the next search crop.
Spiking mem_update modules carry an explicit temporal loop inside one forward; no cross-frame membrane state is exposed.
Tracker crop, resize-factor mapping, window penalty, bbox clipping, and Python list conversion sit outside the neural model graph.

custom_python_or_autograd: No custom C++/CUDA extension, torch.ops call, or pre-existing ONNX/TensorRT artifact was found in the pinned source

confirmed_source_blockers.detail: SPIKETRACK.forward(mode='encoder') calls forward_encoder without its required cache argument, so the inference object has no directly usable single export signature.
Template output and search input use a Python dict of six cache tensors; TensorRT bindings require a flat, ordered tensor interface.
Crop/state/update/window/clip/list conversion are Python tracker operations and are not part of the neural network forward.
The frozen I0 environment contains neither the TensorRT Python package nor ONNX Runtime, and I0 forbids installing packages.

likely_onnx_risks_requiring_experiment: Quant.apply has no explicit ONNX symbolic; the exporter may inline clamp/round or may emit an unsupported Python/autograd node.
mem_update uses shape-dependent Python branches, a temporal Python loop, clone/detach, and indexed tensor assignment output[i] = spike.
Fixed-T tracing can unroll control flow but may silently specialize the graph; exported parity must cover template and search paths.
Nested dictionaries and the two-stage cache interface require an export-only adapter before ONNX can expose stable tensor names.
likely_tensorrt_risks_requiring_experime: TensorRT parsing cannot be assessed until the custom-autograd and cache-interface ONNX risks are resolved.
Any residual Round, Gather, Mod, Scatter/index-write, or dynamic-shape form must be checked against the selected TensorRT parser version.
The six cache tensors need explicit fixed profiles and binding order; tracker-side bbox/crop logic remains on the host unless separately reimplemented.
minimum_I1_experiment: Create export-only adapters for template-to-six-cache and search-plus-six-cache-to-four-decoder-maps; do not change trained modules.
Freeze BS1 FP32, 256x256 crops and explicit cache tensor names/shapes; record eager reference tensors from one locked sequence frame.
Attempt ONNX export and checker validation with no graph rewrite first; capture exact exporter nodes/errors.
If Quant or mem_update blocks export, implement the smallest functionally equivalent export formulation and require eager-versus-ONNX tensor parity before any TensorRT parse.
Only after ONNX parity, parse/build one FP32 TensorRT engine and compare all four decoder maps plus final bbox; no performance claim before parity.
